problem: Stages 3–11 had been planned as one implementation, built ahead of the data they steward. A workflow surface built ahead of its data is designed against an IMAGINED shape of that data. The concrete cost showed up at Stage 2: the review queue posted `{decision, notes}` and never a `provenanceClass`, the ingestion refused, the client checked only the outer `ok`, and every approval moved a source out of the pending queue while producing no evidence row at all.
observedFailure: The review route answered `{ok: true, candidate: {...}, ingestion: {ok: false, error: 'provenanceClass is not set…'}}` and the client reported success.

Sources moved to `approved_*`, counted as admitted, and left the pending queue — with zero evidence rows behind them. An operator working the queue would have watched 41 sources drain into an apparently-admitted corpus containing nothing.
The Stage 8 assignment control asks the operator to type invariant IDs, because when it was written there were no validated invariants to list — a design frozen around an absence.
rootCauses: A stage with no inputs cannot be dry-run, so its refusals, empty states and error paths are all unverified.
A rendered stage reads as progress. A state machine displayed as a single verdict let the operator believe work had happened that had not.
A nested failure result was returned faithfully and never inspected — the outer `ok` was the only thing read.
resolution: Ratified the stage-gated cadence: build only the operator workflow the NEXT stage needs, once the PREVIOUS stage's real outputs exist. Stop between stages and report.
`applyCandidateReviewDecision` REFUSES an ingesting decision with no `provenanceClass` before any write — a named refusal replaces a swallowed failure.
The queue asks for the class where it is required and sends it; the card reads `ingestion.ok` and renders an admitted-but-not-ingested source as the amber half-state it is.
`services/corpusScout/reviewDecision.ts` is the single place a review decision is validated and applied.
rejectedApproaches: Build the Stage 5 (Classify Provenance) queue now — the ratified crystal domain is still empty, so there are no real promoted invariants to classify, and building it would repeat the exact mistake the cadence exists to stop.
Default the `provenanceClass` server-side so the existing client keeps working — that hides the missing decision rather than surfacing it.
